title: Rubisco: the enzyme that fixes CO₂

questions.question: Why do farmers spread so much nitrogen fertiliser on a wheat field?
questions.story: Nitrogen is built into proteins, and one leaf protein dominates: Rubisco, the enzyme that fixes CO₂, holds about 20 % of all the nitrogen in a C₃ leaf. The reason is speed: each active site of Rubisco fixes only about 3 CO₂ per second, where a typical enzyme of central metabolism turns over about 80 times per second, so a leaf needs a great deal of Rubisco to fix CO₂ as fast as light allows.
steps: Rubisco carries out the first step of the cycle: it adds CO₂ to RuBP.
Its turnover number is low: about 3 CO₂ per second per active site, against about 80 s⁻¹ for a typical enzyme of central metabolism.
To fix enough CO₂, a C₃ leaf holds large amounts of Rubisco: about 20 % of its nitrogen.
Nitrogen also goes into chlorophyll, other proteins and DNA: the question is a door, not the whole answer.
